results.reason: Quotes §2.2 automatic five-year renewal and the 270/240-day notice requirement. Calculates the window as June 3 – July 3, 2026, effectively a 30-day window. Explains that missing it locks Harrowgate into a five-year Renewal Term through 2032.

Quotes §3.1 (all glass and PET, any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates) and contrasts it with the term sheet's amber glass/beer/U.S.-Canada scope. Treats out-of-scope purchases as a breach of §3.1, so Harrowgate is bound by the executed text.
Cites Recital C (receipt August 3, 2026). Computes the §5.4 deadline as September 2, 2026, before the September 21 amendment date. Concludes the increase is deemed accepted.

Explains that Amendment §2.1 replaces §11.2, removes recall costs, and limits the indemnity carve-out to §9.1(c) IP claims. States that recall and product-liability claims are now subject to the six-month fee cap.

Identifies new §14.4, which permits assignment without consent to Affiliates or to successors by merger or change of control, notwithstanding §14.3. Notes risk of acquisition by a competitor of Harrowgate. Notes Customer still needs consent under §14.3, making it one-sided.
The Order of Precedence note states §15.2 places written amendments first, so Amendment No. 1 controls over the Supply Agreement.
States the §11.1 cap is 'the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.'
Memo addressed to Partner, with numbered issues. Each issue has a 'Where' citation and a 'Recommended fix.'
Provides specific drafting, including a narrowed §3.1, a restored §11.2, and a revised §14.4, among others.
States the objection window has closed and there is no contractual basis to challenge the increase.
Does not conclude the term sheet governs. It recommends amending §3.1 and treats the current text as binding.
